rationale: The first turn was strong: immediate stop-use and unplug, a correct warning never to open the casing, and well-ordered checks (metal, the side-wall cover panel, cavity paint). The customer then handed over near-conclusive evidence of a burnt, grease-splattered waveguide cover, but the second turn ignored it entirely and fired a generic burning-smell card telling them to get an engineer. Per the ground truth, replacing the clip-on waveguide cover and cleaning the cavity is an acceptable, cheap DIY fix for a known model, with an engineer only if sparking persists; so the escalation is premature and the diagnosis was never named. Nothing unsafe or fabricated, but the homeowner is left without the actual answer their own evidence pointed to.
